text:
Lowest midgrade gas price in Montague County hits $3.39 for week ending July 4
M. W. Reedy
Montague County had one gas station selling midgrade gas at the lowest price of $3.39 per gallon during the week ending July 4, according to customer reports submitted to GasBuddy.
The average reported price of midgrade gas across the county was $3.71 per gallon.
Montague County had four of 17 reported gas stations offering midgrade gas.
Across Texas, the average reported price for a gallon of midgrade gas fell to $3.76, compared to the week before.
AAA listed the national average for regular gasoline at $3.823 per gallonon July 3, down from $4.261 a month earlier but above $3.163 a year earlier. Diesel prices showed a similar pattern, falling to $4.811 from $5.411 a month earlier while remaining above the year-earlier average of $3.689.
The decline followed a volatile spring in energy markets, when analysts linked higher gasoline and diesel prices to rising crude oil prices and concerns about supply disruptions tied to the conflict involving Iran and the Strait of Hormuz.
The U.S. Energy Information Administration said gasoline prices continue to react to both international oil markets and domestic fuel supply conditions. Analysts monitoring the energy market have pointed to refinery utilization rates, U.S. crude oil inventories, OPEC+ production policies and seasonal driving demand as factors influencing fuel costs in 2026, particularly during periods of refinery outages or shipping disruptions affecting global oil supplies.
Gas price data reflects cash payments. Some stations may charge higher prices for credit card transactions due to processing fees, though such surcharges are prohibited in some states and territories.
Data is accurate as of press time, but gas prices have been known to fluctuate on a daily, and even hourly, basis.
Information in this article was obtained from GasBuddy. The source data can be found here.
